gen_risks.description: Delay in Treasury approval could postpone funding confirmation and push back the national rollout schedule.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage Treasury early, secure provisional funding, and design a phased rollout that can start with funded cohorts.
gen_risks.evidence: timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury

gen_risks.description: Schools may lack sufficient space or staffing to deliver the required 30‑minute supervised breakfast provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct capacity assessments, deploy technical estate advisers, and provide additional resources or alternative spaces where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints

gen_risks.description: The internal CRM system may not be operational by the November 2025 target, delaying onboarding of cohort 1 schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate a dedicated development team, adopt agile milestones, run early user testing, and retain a manual onboarding fallback.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum‑viable product from November 2025

gen_risks.description: Lower than expected school participation could reduce the projected benefit‑cost ratio.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement targeted outreach, incentives, and regular monitoring of uptake to adjust engagement tactics promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: forecast for up to 2,250 schools... staggered take‑up assumptions

gen_risks.description: Complexity of the previous funding model may cause confusion and deter mainstream schools from joining.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide clear guidance, webinars, a helpdesk, and simplified documentation for the new funding model.
gen_risks.evidence: variation by disadvantage levels was deemed to be complicated for mainstream schools, resulting in confusion

gen_risks.description: A gap in breakfast provision could occur when the NSBP ends in July 2026 before FBCs are fully operational.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee continuity arrangements, align closure dates, and offer temporary bridging provision where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026

gen_risks.description: Delays in procuring advisers and launching the call‑centre pilot may limit support for schools during rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast‑track procurement using existing frameworks, set firm milestones, and allocate interim support staff if needed.
gen_risks.evidence: procurement process to increase the number of advisers... start commercial processes to begin a call‑centre pilot

gen_risks.description: Supply‑chain disruptions could prevent schools from obtaining food that meets required standards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Qualify multiple suppliers, maintain buffer stocks, and embed contingency clauses in contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards

gen_risks.description: Unexpected inflation or labour‑market cost increases may make the daily funding rates insufficient.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include an inflation contingency in the budget and review area cost adjustments annually.
gen_risks.evidence: area cost adjustment to account for variations in the labour market

gen_risks.description: Delay or amendment to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill could postpone the mandatory duty for schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor parliamentary timetable, engage with legislators, and develop interim guidance for schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state‑funded schools

gen_risks.description: DfE may lack sufficient skilled staff to oversee programme delivery and governance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit or second additional staff, provide targeted training, and leverage external advisors where gaps exist.
gen_risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector

gen_risks.description: Data collection challenges could undermine the robustness of the programme evaluation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pilot the data‑collection system, use the call‑centre support, and implement rigorous data‑quality checks.
gen_risks.evidence: call‑centre pilot to support data collection

gen_risks.description: The £1,000 start‑up grant may be insufficient for essential equipment, training and systems at some schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allow supplemental grant requests and issue clear guidance on cost‑effective procurement options.
gen_risks.evidence: £1,000 start‑up grant to cover one‑off costs... Schools are provided with initial funding to cover essential equipment, training and systems

gen_risks.description: Keeping special‑school funding rates unchanged could raise equity concerns compared with mainstream schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor equity outcomes and consider adjustments in subsequent funding rounds.
gen_risks.evidence: At special schools, the funding rate is... remaining the same from the EA scheme to year 1

gen_risks.description: If the evaluation is not perceived as independent, credibility of impact findings may be questioned.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contract an independent evaluator, publish methodology, and ensure transparent governance of the evaluation process.
gen_risks.evidence: evaluation will be independently commissioned and run from 2026 to 2028

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
